item.title: Rugby House set for facelift
item.description: FIJI Rugby is set to restore pride in the home of the national game with a facelift for Rugby House and the High-Performance Unit (HPU) Gym through a new partnership with Dulux Fiji. Dulux Fiji will serve as the Official Paint Partner, with refurbishment expected to begin in the coming months.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI Rugby is set to restore pride in the home of the national game with a facelift for Rugby House and the High-Performance Unit (HPU) Gym through a new partnership with Dulux Fiji.

Dulux Fiji will serve as the Official Paint Partner, with refurbishment expected to begin in the coming months.

This project is more than a fresh coat of paint; it aims to improve Fiji Rugby’s working environment and strengthen the organisation’s foundations.

CEO Koli Sewabu said Rugby House must reflect the pride and professionalism of its staff and players.

“Every meaningful transformation begins with small but deliberate actions, and this is one of those moments,” Sewabu said.

“Rugby House is the heart of our organisation, and we want it to reflect the pride, professionalism and ambition of Fijian rugby.”

The refurbishment will upgrade facilities used daily by players, coaches, and staff preparing for national and international campaigns.

Sewabu emphasised that while on-field performance is important, behind-the-scenes work is equally crucial for Fiji Rugby’s long-term success.

He described the Dulux partnership as an investment in creating a more professional and inspiring environment.

Dulux Fiji CEO Roshan Singh said the company was honoured to support Fiji’s national sport, calling rugby a source of “pride, unity and inspiration” for the nation.

“We are honoured to play a small part in supporting Fiji Rugby by helping create spaces that reflect the pride and passion associated with our national sport.”

The refurbishment marks a key step in Fiji Rugby’s efforts to build a stronger organisation and renew Rugby House, the home of Fijian rugby.

item.title: A historic last four for Lomary
item.description: LOMARY Secondary School has qualified for the Under-18 Weet-Bix Raluve semi-finals for the first time in the school’s history following a 38-5 victory over Bua Central College last Saturday at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva. Assistant coach Samuela Gucake said the achievement was a significant milestone for the side, which had waited several years for an opportunity to reach the semifinals.
item.content:encoded:
LOMARY Secondary School has qualified for the Under-18 Weet-Bix Raluve semi-finals for the first time in the school’s history following a 38-5 victory over Bua Central College last Saturday at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

Assistant coach Samuela Gucake said the achievement was a significant milestone for the side, which had waited several years for an opportunity to reach the semifinals.

Gucake also acknowledged Bua Central, who travelled from Vanua Levu to compete in the competition.

“This is the first-time for us to be at the semifinal after so many years of competing in the girls’ division,” Gucake said.

He said the team would now focus on improving its execution ahead of next week’s semifinal, where the competition would become tougher.

“I believe we need to perfect our execution. We know that the competition will only get tougher.

Gucake said some players were playing rugby for the first time, making teamwork and preparation important heading into the semifinal.

He said the message to the players before the match was simple, give 100 per cent effort and have no excuses, regardless of the result.

Gucake thanked supporters who turned up for the match and called on more fans to support the team next week.

“We are calling on all the supporters next week to come out in numbers. Come in your blue colours and let’s support the girls,” he said.

item.title: Deans, Raluve semis set
item.description: FOUR Vodafone Super Deans and Weet-Bix Raluve semi-finals will be played alongside the Vodafone Fijiana XVs second Test match against South Africa in Churchill Park, Lautoka. The Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Interim committee, with the support of the Ministry of Education and Fiji Rakavi Football Union, has confirmed a two-venue program for the national semi-finals.
item.content:encoded:
FOUR Vodafone Super Deans and Weet-Bix Raluve semi-finals will be played alongside the Vodafone Fijiana XVs second Test match against South Africa in Churchill Park, Lautoka.

The Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Interim committee, with the support of the Ministry of Education and Fiji Rakavi Football Union, has confirmed a two-venue program for the national semi-finals.

The arrangement will give secondary school students the opportunity to play in front of a large crowd and share the stage with the Fijiana XV.

Interim committee representative Biu Colati said the program aimed at strengthening the development pathway for secondary schools rugby.

“Our priority has always been to provide the best possible experience for our student-athletes while continuing to strengthen the development pathway for secondary school rugby,” Colati said.

The Churchill Park program will begin with the Vodafone Super Deans under-14 semi-final between Ratu Navula College and Ratu Kadavulevu School, followed by the U19 clash between Ratu Navula College and Lelean Memorial School.

The Weet-Bix Raluve U16 semifinal between Sigatoka Methodist College and St Vincent College will also be played at Churchill Park.

The Fijiana XV will meet the Springbok women at 1pm in the second Test match, with Fiji aiming to level the series and retain the trophy.

The final school match of the day will be the Vodafone Super Deans U18 semi-final between Suva Grammar School and Ra High School. Ra has enjoyed a strong campaign after entering the Northern Division playoffs as the Western division’s fourth ranked qualifier. The remaining semi-finals will be played at the HFC Bank Stadium, Buckhurst ground 1 and Bidesi ground.

Confirmed semi-final fixtures for all grades; U14 – Ratu Navula College (RNC) v Ratu Kadavulevu School (west); Queen Victoria School (QVS) v Mahatma Ghandi Memorial (MGM) U15 – Lelean Memorial School (LMS) v Marist Brothers High School (MBHS); QVS v RKS; U16 – Nasinu Secondary School (NSS) v Suva Grammar School (SGS), QVS v MGM; U17 – Ba Methodist v RKS, QVS v SGS; U19 RNC v LMS(west); RKS v Navatu Secondary School; Raluve U16 – Sigatoka Methodist v St Vincent College (west); Adi Cakobau v NSS; Raluve U18 MGM v Adi Cakobau, Sila Central v Lomary Secondary; Deans U18 – SGS v Ra High (west), LMS v NSS

item.title: Lal retains 10km title, eyes Pacific Games
item.description: AVIKASH Lal overcame fatigue and limited preparation to claim the individual 10km title at the Suva Marathon last Saturday, as he continues to build towards his goal of representing Fiji at the next Pacific Games. Lal said the victory was challenging after a busy travel schedule, which included returning from Los Angeles before travelling from Sigatoka to Suva for the event.
item.content:encoded:
AVIKASH Lal overcame fatigue and limited preparation to claim the individual 10km title at the Suva Marathon last Saturday, as he continues to build towards his goal of representing Fiji at the next Pacific Games.

Lal said the victory was challenging after a busy travel schedule, which included returning from Los Angeles before travelling from Sigatoka to Suva for the event.

“It was a tiring race for me. Last night I came to Sigatoka, drove all the way to Suva and I only had two hours rest,” Lal said.

“Two days before this I flew to LA and came back with no rest. I came to enjoy the race and I won the race. I feel good.”

The win marked Lal’s second consecutive victory in the same event, after also finishing first last year.

He said while there was limited competition this year, the cooler weather conditions made the race enjoyable.

“I feel amazing because I won the same race last year. Today I had no competition, but the weather was pretty cool, so I’m enjoying it,” he said.

Lal said his next major target is to earn selection to represent Fiji at next year’s Pacific Games, with the Suva Marathon forming part of his preparation.

“My next big dream is to represent Fiji in the Pacific Games next year. Hopefully I can come back again. I’m just building up for next year,” he said.

He encouraged others working towards fitness goals to remain committed, saying discipline and self-belief were key to achieving success.

“You have to sacrifice. It’s all in your mind and you have to be your own inspiration. Keep training, keep eating well and enjoy. Life is short,” Lal said.

The 2027 Pacific Games will be held in Tahiti.

item.title: Tigers warn of Silktails threat in Fiji
item.description: WEST Tigers head coach Shane Sultana has warned that the Kaiviti Silktails remain a dangerous side despite their 32-14 defeat in Round 23 of the Jersey Flegg Cup competition at Churchill Park in Lautoka on Saturday. The Tigers secured the victory, but Sultana said playing against a Fijian side in Fiji was never an easy assignment, particularly because of the physicality, weather and unpredictable
item.content:encoded:
WEST Tigers head coach Shane Sultana has warned that the Kaiviti Silktails remain a dangerous side despite their 32-14 defeat in Round 23 of the Jersey Flegg Cup competition at Churchill Park in Lautoka on Saturday.

The Tigers secured the victory, but Sultana said playing against a Fijian side in Fiji was never an easy assignment, particularly because of the physicality, weather and unpredictable style of play.

“We knew what to expect. The common word we use when we come over here is that the game is going to be brutal,” Sultana said.

“Brutal in contact, brutal weather, brutal environment. The Fijian team, they don’t give up. They don’t go away. They just play ad-lib football and play with a lot of opportunity, and that made it hard for us.”

Sultana said the Tigers had to be disciplined with their field position because the Silktails could punish them if given opportunities in attacking areas.

“One thing I stress to the boys is when you play Fiji, you have to make them start football down that end. You cannot let them start up here. If you start them up here, they’re going to hurt you all day,” he said.

Despite the result, Sultana praised the Silktails, saying their position on the competition ladder did not reflect their ability.

item.title: Hill eyes possible return to the ring | Rising star’s challenge tempts former champion
item.description: FORMER Fiji welterweight champion Winston Hill has opened the door to a comeback in the ring after local knockout artist Isikeli ‘The Bullet’ Senidoko publicly challenged him following his victory over Filise Nabua. Hill, who retired from the sport to focus on business and family life, admitted the challenge caught him by surprise as he watched the fight from the crowd.
item.content:encoded:
FORMER Fiji welterweight champion Winston Hill has opened the door to a comeback in the ring after local knockout artist Isikeli ‘The Bullet’ Senidoko publicly challenged him following his victory over Filise Nabua.

Hill, who retired from the sport to focus on business and family life, admitted the challenge caught him by surprise as he watched the fight from the crowd.

“Senidoko has a very interesting character in local professional boxing,” Hill said.

“He lacks discipline but comes out with raw talent and ability.”

Hill said he simply acknowledged the challenge with a wave but stressed that any decision to fight would first be discussed with his wife and management team.

While content with life outside the ring, the former champion remains confident he has what it takes to beat the rising contender.

“I wouldn’t say it’s going to be hard. It’s going to be an easy fight, a walk in the park,” Hill said.

“I don’t even need to fight Senidoko under the bright lights in front of a big crowd. I can invite him to my gym, we can put on the boxing gloves and I’ll give him an … whooping. It’s as easy as that.”

Hill admitted he was “a little out of shape” but believed he would still have too much class and experience for Senidoko.

No agreement has been reached, with Hill confirming no contracts have been signed.

“The boxing business has to get me out of retirement. I don’t have any urgency or need to fight Senidoko. It’s what he wants and what the people want to see, but it’s not on my priority list.”

However, Hill said should both camps eventually reach an agreement, he would fully commit to training.

“If we do sign the contract, then I’ll be taking it seriously and he’ll have to get very serious if we are to fight.”

item.title: Fiu leads female tennis push
item.description: AT a time when women are making greater strides in sport, the 20-year-old Repeka Fiu is hoping her journey in tennis will inspire more females to pick up the racquet and step onto the court. Fiu is currently the only female tennis coach based in Suva, a role she has embraced over the past two years while continuing to develop herself as a player.
item.content:encoded:
AT a time when women are making greater strides in sport, the 20-year-old Repeka Fiu is hoping her journey in tennis will inspire more females to pick up the racquet and step onto the court.

Fiu is currently the only female tennis coach based in Suva, a role she has embraced over the past two years while continuing to develop herself as a player.

Her journey with tennis began seriously in 2023, after the COVID-19 pandemic, and she describes the experience as one that has shaped her both personally and professionally.

“My journey in Tennis Fiji has been a really good one, a fruitful one I would say,” Fiu said.

“The sport has helped me a lot in my journey, has kept me healthy and has been a really good sport.”

While coaching has become her passion, Fiu believes there is still room for more women to become involved in tennis, especially in coaching roles.

She said many female players felt more comfortable learning from female coaches, but opportunities remained limited.

“From my two years of coaching female players, they’re more comfortable with female coaches. It’s sad that there’s only one female coach here in Suva,” she said.

Fiu hopes more women will take up coaching and help create a stronger pathway for female participation in tennis.

Away from coaching, Fiu continues to challenge herself as a player. She reached the semi-finals of the women’s open category at last year’s Vodafone Suva Open Tennis Tournament and has set her sights on going further this year.

“I’m hoping to at least make it to the finals,” she said.

The fourth Vodafone Suva Open Tennis Tournament will be held from August 21 to 24 at the Victoria Tennis Courts, with players from Fiji, Samoa, the Solomon Islands and Australia expected to compete.

The tournament will also introduce new junior categories, including Under-7, Under-8 and Under-10 divisions, as tennis continues to grow among young players.

For Fiu, the goal remains simple — to encourage more people, especially women and girls, to give tennis a chance.

“You wouldn’t know if you like the sport until you try it,” she said.

item.title: Ba reigns
item.description: JOHN Orobulu scored a hat-trick as Dayals Sawmillers Ba FC ended a seven-year wait for the Extra Premier League title with a commanding 6-0 victory over Tailevu Naitasiri at the 4R Stadium, Govind Park, Ba, yesterday. The Men in Black produced a composed and dominant performance, controlling possession and showing their strength in both defence and attack from the opening whistle.
item.content:encoded:
JOHN Orobulu scored a hat-trick as Dayals Sawmillers Ba FC ended a seven-year wait for the Extra Premier League title with a commanding 6-0 victory over Tailevu Naitasiri at the 4R Stadium, Govind Park, Ba, yesterday.

The Men in Black produced a composed and dominant performance, controlling possession and showing their strength in both defence and attack from the opening whistle.

Orobulu opened the scoring in the 39th minute after Ba applied sustained pressure on the Tailevu Naitasiri defence.

Ba maintained their composure and went into halftime with a 1-0 lead.

They returned from the break with greater intensity and quickly extended their advantage.

A foul inside the penalty area in the 49th minute handed Ba a penalty, which Praneel Naidu calmly converted to make it 2-0.

Ba continued to dominate and Orobulu struck again to score his second goal of the match.

Vilitati Kautoga then added another goal as Ba continued to dismantle the Tailevu Naitasiri defence.

Orobulu completed his hat-trick to further underline Ba’s dominance before Shazil rounded off the scoring with the sixth goal.

The victory ended Ba’s seven-year wait for the Extra Premier League title and added another major trophy to their cabinet after their Fiji FACT triumph earlier this season.

Ba coach Ravinesh Kumar praised his players for delivering when it mattered most.

“I’m happy with the boys. They knew a win today would make us win the title, so the boys delivered,” Kumar said.

The victory sparked celebrations in Ba as the Men in Black finally reclaimed the league crown after seven years.

The emphatic 6-0 victory not only ended Ba FC’s seven-year wait for the Extra Premier League title but also solidified their status as a dominant force in Fijian football.

This triumph adds to their impressive haul this year, complementing their 2026 BiC Fiji FACT Champions trophy won in Labasa earlier this season.

With such a strong finish to the year, Ba FC has set a high standard for themselves and will be a team to watch in the upcoming seasons.
